# Tests known to fail on main. Generated by scripts/check_test_ratchet.py --update.
#
# CI fails only when a failure appears that is NOT listed here, so this file
# is a ratchet: it may shrink freely, and should only grow with a deliberate
# decision. Prune an entry as soon as its test passes again.
#
# CAUTION for the entries below: they pass on a developer machine and fail in
# CI, so a local run reports "8 baseline failure(s) now pass -- prune them".
# Do not. Pruning on that basis turns CI red again. Verify against a checkout
# containing only tracked files first:
#
#     git ls-files -z | tar -czf /tmp/t.tgz --null -T - && \
#       mkdir /tmp/ci && tar -xzf /tmp/t.tgz -C /tmp/ci && \
#       cd /tmp/ci && python scripts/check_test_ratchet.py
#
# The entries below all share one cause: they build a Flow chain, which needs an
# installed generator or vulnerability catalog, and `outputs/` is gitignored. A
# developer checkout has one -- 87 flag-node-generators in one working tree -- and
# CI has none, so `_pick_flag_chain_nodes` finds nothing eligible and the routes
# answer 422.
#
# They are recorded rather than stubbed because they need differently shaped
# fakes: some want flag-generators, others want vulnerability names drawn from a
# real catalog. A single fixture is not enough -- one attempt broke a test that
# was passing. The durable fix is a small tracked fixture catalog installed by
# the workflow, which would let every entry here be pruned at once.
#
# Recorded count: 8
